title: Ring anchor fit: move ring anchors into the grooves by one global, smooth energy (fit_ring_anchors, Shift+G)
user-messages:
> aRingNearlyOppositeTheGrooveStillMovesIntoIt expects a ring nearly opposite a groove to reach it. The planned groove term only pulls within a groove’s width, so either coverage has to carry the ring there or the groove cost needs a wider basin (valley curvature smoothed over a reach). The plan lists this as unsettled.

the energy needs to be global
description:
Move the anchors of every ring and bisector on a surface into the grooves, or to the middle of their region where there is no groove, by minimising one global, smooth energy. This is the `fit_ring_anchors` node and the ring tool's Shift+G key, split out of the stroke-segmentation worktree (CRAW-105), where it was built without a ticket.

## What exists

Moved here from the craw-105 worktree: `RingAnchorFit` (the energy, the least-squares step, the accept/reject loop), `AnchoredRings` (retraces a ring through moved anchors, makes bisectors follow), `RingBlend`, the `fit_ring_anchors` node, `AnchorGrooveFit` (Shift+G in the ring tool), `RingAnchorFitTest` and its 13 `ring_fit_*` fixtures, and two looks in the ring scene (groove bottoms, what each vertex pays).

## What is wrong with it

The energy today: every vertex pays the square root of its distance along mesh edges to the nearest ring, and a vertex over the crease threshold pays 1000 times more. Problems:

- The groove weight is a threshold, so depth is ignored and the energy look is blocky.
- Distance is Dijkstra along edges, so its level sets follow the mesh and it jumps as a ring moves.
- The square root has an infinitely steep cusp at the ring, so accept and reject near a groove are decided by which vertices the trace happens to hit.
- Constants are in mean edge lengths, so they depend on mesh density.
- Length is only checked when accepting a move; the solve never proposes a straighter ring.
- Each vertex belongs wholly to one ring, so a ring nearest two empty grooves hides the second from every other ring.
- The energy looks are not recomputed after a fit step or after a ring is moved by hand.

## The planned energy

Full equation, symbol table, necessary parts and test cases: `ring_fit_energy_plan.md` at the root of the ai-workspace repo. In short: every point of the surface pays a smooth concave cost of its geodesic distance to the nearest ring (a soft minimum over the rings), weighted continuously by how groove-like the point is; each ring pays for its own length and bend at full price on smooth surface and almost nothing in a groove. Distance is by the heat method (Crane, Weischedel, Wardetzky 2013). The energy has no groove objects: the surface enters only through one field.

## Related

- CRAW-82 (settle a crease-mode draft's anchors into the valleys) asks for the same result for one draft ring. Decide whether this ticket replaces it.
- CRAW-105 (stroke segmentation) must land first: this work reads fields it adds.
definition-of-done:
1. Every unit test passes: RingAnchorFitTest's eleven existing cases unchanged in what they assert, plus the new cases in the testing plan.
2. The ring scene's energy look shows the planned energy and is smooth: no blocks following a crease threshold or the mesh edges. A screenshot under tmp/ shows it.
3. The look updates after each step of the fit and after a ring is moved by hand, through one general look-refresh hook that the region and part looks use too.
4. Every constant the energy and the solve use is listed on this ticket for the user to decide.
5. A launch.json entry and a screenshot under tmp/ show a fixture before and after the fit.
testing-plan:
1. The eleven existing RingAnchorFitTest cases (grooved torus, bisectors, horned sphere).
2. New: grooves at 0 and 60 degrees, rings at 30 and 200 degrees; one ring ends in each groove.
3. New: a slanted ring with half its anchors near each of two grooves; expected result not decided (see unknowns).
4. New: the same slanted ring with two trenches joining the grooves away from where the ring crosses; the ring turns so its crossings lie in the trenches and every anchor stands in a groove or a trench.
5. Unit test of the heat-method distance on a shape with a known answer (a sphere or a flat grid).
todos: Heat-method geodesic distance field over the surface, factored once per mesh
A general look-refresh hook in SurfaceLook / SurfaceLooks, used by the region, part and energy looks
Swap the energy, keeping the eleven existing tests
Anchors that can slide along their ring, then the three new test cases

After stroke segmentation (CRAW-105) lands and this worktree syncs: AnchorGrooveFit must again skip rings drawn as lines, by adding confirmed.curve < 0 and confirmed.stroke == null to its ring filter. The two conditions were dropped so this worktree compiles on master, which has no drawn rings.

RingAnchorFit.solve is 166 lines and the edit hook asks for under 150. The dead field term (FIELD_WEIGHT 0) and the groove-bottom search account for more than that; the user said to leave them in place for now.
The look refreshes after Shift+G finishes and after a hand edit, not after each step: the fit runs inside one key press. Showing each step means running one round per frame.
AnchoredRings.look has no caller now that the looks read the ring tool's live rings.
unknowns: The slanted ring with half its anchors near each of two grooves: does the whole ring go into one groove (recommended), or stay split? The user is not sure yet; build the fixture and show what the energy does.
Whether one setting of the constants passes the slanted-ring test and the trench test together. If none does, the energy needs another change, not a workaround.
Does this ticket replace CRAW-82 (settle a crease-mode draft's anchors into the valleys)?
The groove-bottom search and the field term (weight 0) are dead today. The user said to leave them in place for now.

Constants for the user to decide (all in RingAnchorFit): GROOVE_WEIGHT 1000 (a deep groove point against a smooth one), POWER 0.5 (how the cost grows with distance), LENGTH_WEIGHT 0.1 (tried 0.03 and 0.1; the same 9 of 11 pass with both), BEND_WEIGHT 1e-4, COST_SMOOTHING_EDGES 0. The groove price of length reuses SurfaceCreases.GROOVE_COST_OF_LENGTH 0.05. The soft minimum and the heat's flow time use the mean edge, which the mesh fixes.

The cost is not smoothed at the ring (COST_SMOOTHING_EDGES 0), unlike the plan. With it smoothed over one edge, a ring in one groove was drawn up to three cross-sections out of it by the other, uncovered groove; unsmoothed it sits exactly. The look is still smooth; only the cost has a corner on the ring itself.

Still failing 1: bisector_smooth_rings. The bisector lies in its groove except its end on ring_00, two tube sides off. That end gains almost nothing by sliding, because the ring it stands on already covers the groove points there.

Still failing 2: two_grooves_crease. In crease mode one anchor ends 36 degrees out and the fit hits its round limit. It failed on master before any change too (4.5 degrees off), and the crease tracer was rewritten in CRAW-105, so it may need that work to land first.

Nearest both fails because the soft nearest-ring choice is over one mean edge, which is nearly a hard choice: the empty groove never pulls the far ring. Making it pull needs the softness to be about the spacing between rings, which is a picked number.
changes-made: 2026-11-12, first session in the craw-106 worktree. Baseline on master before any change: 8 of the 11 RingAnchorFitTest cases pass; both bisector cases and the crease-mode two-groove case fail. Then: (1) SurfaceHeatDistance, a heat-method geodesic distance field factored once per surface, with SurfaceHeatDistanceTest (three sphere cases, every vertex within one mean edge of the great-circle distance). (2) SurfaceLook.revision: a field look names a revision number and ModelScene reads the field again when it changes; the two fit looks read the ring tool's live rings through RingTool.grooveFit and refresh on ringRevision. (3) RingAnchorFit's energy replaced: the groove weight is continuous (1 + 1000 x valley strength), distance is each ring's heat distance with a soft minimum over a mean edge, the cost is distance to the power 0.5 in surface widths, and each ring pays for its length and in-surface bend, 0.05 of the price where it runs in a groove. (4) After the solved whole-ring moves stall, each anchor alone tries every vertex next to it, across and along its ring, and the two alternate until neither gains. Result: 9 of 11 pass, and every grooved ring that passes has all its anchors exactly on the groove. Screenshots tmp/craw-106-energy-look-as-drawn.png and tmp/craw-106-energy-look-fitted.png show the look smooth and refreshed after Shift+G.

2026-11-12, later: the three new cases are in RingAnchorFitTest with fixtures ring_fit_two_grooves_one_ring_nearest_both, ring_fit_slanted_ring and ring_fit_slanted_ring_trenches. All three fail. Nearest both: the midway ring takes the 60 degree groove, with two inside anchors 6 degrees short of it; the far ring moves 2.5 degrees and never comes round to the empty groove. Slanted ring: it stays split, three anchors by each groove, four of the six one or two cross-sections off the bottoms. Trenches: the ring keeps crossing over the top and bottom of the tube as drawn and does not turn to the trenches. ROUNDS raised from 200 to 1000 so each case runs until nothing gains (205 to 224 rounds); 9 of the 11 older cases still pass.

2026-11-13: added fixture ring_fit_tree_partly_in_groove and the test theRestOfARingPartlyInATreesGrooveIsFittedIntoTheNearerBranch. A trunk groove round the outer half of the tube forks at the top and bottom into two branches that end short of the inside; the ring's outer half is drawn in the trunk and its inner half between the branches, 3 and 6 degrees from the nearer branch's bottom. The test fails with the fit as it stands: the anchor beside the branch stays where drawn (2.25 degrees) where the branch runs at 5.21. Picture of the fixture's groove strength: tmp/craw-106-tree-fixture.png. The design has moved on from the coverage energy; ai-workspace ring_fit_energy_plan.md holds the current plan (the nudge rule), none of which is built.

2026-11-13, later: RingAnchorFit's energy replaced again, at the user's direction. Each ring now pays the mean, along itself, of the heat-method distance to the nearest groove no other ring lies in; a groove is the bottom line of a band of full groove strength. GROOVE_WEIGHT, POWER, LENGTH_WEIGHT, BEND_WEIGHT, COST_SMOOTHING_EDGES and the use of GROOVE_COST_OF_LENGTH are removed, with the coverage, length and bend terms. Every ring now travels to a groove from anywhere, a quarter-turn and nearly opposite included. 3 of the 15 fit tests pass; most failures are one or two anchors two or three cross-sections off the bottom line.
